review.notes: Machine-drafted by an AI model; awaiting native-speaker review. House style: moderate Bokmål with three genders (ei/-a for feminine nouns, en/-en masculine, et/-et neuter), weak past in -et, neuter definite plural in -ene, sju and tjue, "ble", "ga". An invented invitation letter from a local congregation; no real church is named. The register is warm and formal-friendly ("Kjære venner", "Hilsen").

english.source: drafted with the text; not reviewed

sentences.text: Kjære venner,
sentences.english: Dear friends,

sentences.text: Vi inviterer dere til gudstjeneste i kirka vår på søndag klokka elleve.
sentences.english: We invite you to the service in our church on Sunday at eleven o'clock.

sentences.text: Alle er velkomne, gamle og små. Vi inviterer alle, og alle er velkomne.
sentences.english: Everyone is welcome, old and small. We invite everyone, and everyone is welcome.

sentences.text: Etter gudstjenesten drikker vi kaffe og spiser kake sammen. Der kan dere treffe folk i menigheten.
sentences.english: After the service we drink coffee and eat cake together. There you can meet the people of the congregation.

sentences.text: Hvis dere har spørsmål, kan dere ringe til presten. Han heter Hansen.
sentences.english: If you have questions, you can call the pastor. His name is Hansen.

sentences.text: Vi håper å se dere!
sentences.english: We hope to see you!

sentences.text: Hilsen menigheten
sentences.english: Greetings from the congregation

sentences.text: Sam har fått brevet. Han leser det for Anna og Lars.
sentences.english: Sam has received the letter. He reads it to Anna and Lars.

sentences.text: Kirka inviterer oss til gudstjeneste på søndag.
sentences.english: The church invites us to the service on Sunday.
sentences.speaker: sam

sentences.text: Vi går i kirka hver søndag, men det er bra å få et brev.
sentences.english: We go to church every Sunday, but it is good to get a letter.
sentences.speaker: ana

sentences.text: Alle er velkomne, sier brevet. Det er en bra menighet.
sentences.english: Everyone is welcome, says the letter. It is a good congregation.
sentences.speaker: luis

sentences.text: Jeg vil gjerne treffe flere folk. Jeg har mange venner, men jeg vil ha flere.
sentences.english: I would like to meet more people. I have many friends, but I want more.
sentences.speaker: sam

sentences.text: Du kan invitere Marta og Nils. De er også velkomne.
sentences.english: You can invite Marta and Nils. They are welcome too.
sentences.speaker: ana

sentences.text: Ja, det gjør jeg. Jeg ringer til Marta i kveld.
sentences.english: Yes, I will. I will call Marta this evening.
sentences.speaker: sam

sentences.text: På søndag kom mange folk til kirka. Alle var velkomne, og alle var glade.
sentences.english: On Sunday many people came to the church. Everyone was welcome, and everyone was happy.

sentences.text: Presten ba, og menigheten sang. Sam sang med, og han var glad.
sentences.english: The pastor prayed, and the congregation sang. Sam sang along, and he was happy.

sentences.text: Etter gudstjenesten drakk de kaffe og spiste kake. Sam traff mange nye folk.
sentences.english: After the service they drank coffee and ate cake. Sam met many new people.

sentences.text: En gammel dame sa til ham: «Velkommen, Sam! Vi har hørt om deg.»
sentences.english: An old lady said to him: "Welcome, Sam! We have heard about you."

sentences.text: Sam ble glad. Han tenkte: «Jeg er ikke alene i Norge. Jeg har en menighet.»
sentences.english: Sam became glad. He thought: "I am not alone in Norway. I have a congregation."

sentences.text: Han skrev et brev til menigheten og takket for invitasjonen.
sentences.english: He wrote a letter to the congregation and thanked them for the invitation.

sentences.text: Marta og Nils var også i kirka. De satt hos Sam, og de sang sammen.
sentences.english: Marta and Nils were also in the church. They sat with Sam, and they sang together.

sentences.text: I menigheten kjenner alle folk. De har tvil og spørsmål, men de er trygge. Svaret er ikke alltid lett.
sentences.english: In the congregation everyone knows people. They have doubt and ask questions, but they feel safe. The answer is not always easy.

sentences.text: Sam leser begge. Først leser han bokmål, og så leser han nynorsk. Han vil forstå dialekter, som Marta snakker.
sentences.english: Sam reads both. First he reads Bokmål, and then he reads Nynorsk. He wants to understand dialects, like Marta speaks.

sentences.text: Folk hørte at Anna kanskje ville flytte til Oslo. Nils skrev om fiskere som bor nær havet og lager tørrfisk.
sentences.english: People heard that Anna might want to move to Oslo. Nils wrote about fishermen who live near the sea and make dried fish.
